_description: Part 16 - the site's own internal search index (this search/ directory) is explicitly NOT Google's index, and this file's whole job is drawing that line precisely so a future implementation never accidentally lets internal search create indexable-by-Google URL proliferation. Every noindex/canonical mechanism referenced below is taken directly from the EXISTING SEO round's own findings (seo/robots-contract.json, seo/site-seo-manifest.json) - not re-decided here, per rule #10.
coreDistinction: search/search-index.json exists so THIS SITE's own search feature can find and rank its own 520 documents for a visitor typing a query on this site. It has no relationship to Googlebot, no relationship to sitemap.xml, and none of its fields (searchAliases, synonyms, ranking scores) are SEO signals - they only ever run client-side (or server-side, per search-performance-report.json's recommendation) in response to an actual visitor's actual query. Confusing the two would mean treating every possible query string as if it deserved its own crawlable, indexable URL - which is exactly the failure mode this file rules out below.

hypotheticalSearchResultsPage.assumedRoute: /search?q=... (or /tr/search?q=..., or an equivalent path - the exact route is a future implementation detail; this contract applies to whatever path an eventual query-driven results page uses).
hypotheticalSearchResultsPage.indexabilityPolicy: NOINDEX, always, unconditionally - `robots: { index: false, follow: true }` on the results page's own Metadata, the SAME real, already-proven mechanism seo/robots-contract.json documents for the 5 journey-merged pages (verified as the codebase's existing, correct pattern for a page that must remain crawlable-and-linkable but never appear in search results itself). `follow: true` (not `follow: false`) is deliberate and consistent with that same existing pattern - a results page's outbound links to real documents (calculators, journeys, ab-tests, etc.) should still be crawlable, only the results page's OWN URL should never surface in Google.
hypotheticalSearchResultsPage.reasoning: A query-parameter-driven results page has, by construction, effectively infinite possible URLs (one per distinct query string + filter combination) - indexing even a fraction of them would create massive, low-value URL surface competing with (and diluting authority from) the site's own real, canonical calculator/journey/ab-test/blog pages that already have carefully-built SEO contracts (see seo/ directory) for exactly those queries. A search RESULTS page is a navigation aid for a human, not new content Google should discover independently - the actual content those results point to is already indexed under its own real URL.

sitemapPolicy.rule: The search results route (and any of its query-string variations) must NEVER be added to src/app/sitemap.ts - consistent with seo/sitemap-contract.json's own scope, which enumerates only real, canonical content pages, and with site-seo-manifest.json's own convention of explicitly marking noindex page families as `"sitemap": false` (see the journey-merged entry, the same pattern this file's hypotheticalSearchResultsPage extends to a search-results route).
sitemapPolicy.verification: src/app/sitemap.ts was already audited this round (build-search-index.mjs / the prior SEO round both cross-checked it) - it enumerates only the 5 real corpora's own canonical routes plus static pages; adding a query-string-driven route to it would be a new, deliberate change this contract explicitly forbids without a separate, explicit decision.

urlParameterProliferationGuard.risk: Even with the results page itself set to noindex, an implementation detail could still accidentally create a proliferation problem: if individual FILTERED result-page URLs (e.g. /search?q=cac&type=calculator) are ever treated as separately shareable/bookmarkable/linked-to permalinks, each one is still just as noindex as the base page (noindex is set on the page/route, not per-query-string, so this is automatically inherited) - but they should also never be linked TO from anywhere else on the site in a way that implies they're real content (e.g. never placed in an internal 'related searches' link block that functions like real navigation) - that would create real, crawlable, low-value internal links even though the target itself stays noindex.
urlParameterProliferationGuard.rule: Internal links to specific documents (calculators, journeys, etc.) must always link to that document's own real canonical URL (per seo/canonical-contract.json) - NEVER to a /search?q=... URL that happens to resolve to that document as its top result. Search is an entry point INTO the real URL structure, never a substitute link target for it.

canonicalTagOnResultsPage: If the results page renders any canonical tag at all (optional, since it's noindex - a page correctly marked noindex doesn't strictly need a canonical, but rendering a self-referencing one is harmless and is the existing codebase's general habit per seo/canonical-contract.json), it must point at itself with the query stripped or at the site's real search-entry surface, NEVER at one of the individual result documents (that would incorrectly imply the search page and a specific calculator/journey/etc. are the same content, undermining that document's own already-established canonical from seo/canonical-contract.json).
alignmentConfirmation: This file introduces no new noindex/canonical/sitemap DECISION beyond what seo/robots-contract.json and seo/site-seo-manifest.json already established for the journey-merged case - it only extends the SAME existing pattern to a hypothetical future route this round's search-data work makes newly relevant, per rule #10's explicit instruction not to re-decide indexability in the search layer.
